saints.name: St. John Chrysostom
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The "golden-mouthed" preacher of Antioch and archbishop of Constantinople, whose eloquence and courage cost him exile…
biography: Born at Antioch about 349, John was trained in rhetoric and asceticism and ordained a priest, winning fame as the greatest preacher of the Greek Church — "Chrysostom," the golden-mouthed. Made archbishop of Constantinople in 398, he reformed the clergy, aided the poor, and rebuked the extravagance of the court.

His plain preaching against vice in high places earned the enmity of the empress and of jealous bishops, who twice drove him into exile. He died on the road in 407 with the words "Glory to God for all things." A Doctor of the Church, he is honoured East and West.
saints.knownFor: His matchless preaching and his fearless defence of the poor and the Gospel.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 13 September
